🇲🇽🔍 <u>16,414 Missing People Found, Experts Brought In to Audit the Registry</u>

Mexico's Interior Ministry reports 16,414 people located under the National Search Strategy: 6,939 through the Unified Identity Platform, 4,788 with the states, 3,473 via immediate search alerts and 1,214 in field searches. Rosa Icela Rodríguez is bringing in specialists from USC, Maryland, UNAM, ITAM and CIESAS to analyze the national registry and clean up its data.

🇲🇽💰 <u>Congress Approves 2027 Revenue Law: 10.6 Trillion Pesos</u>

Mexico's Chamber of Deputies passed the 2027 Revenue Law 331–118: 10.6 trillion pesos to fund public spending, 6.2 trillion of it from taxes, with no new taxes. The PRIAN bench complained about 1.7 trillion in borrowing. These are the same parties that turned Fobaproa's bank bailout into public debt Mexicans are still paying off.

🇲🇽🚆 "A total investment of 8 trillion 400 billion pesos. Not to brag, but never before seen in a six-year term." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, 50th anniversary of the Business Coordinating Council (CCE), Mexico City, Oct 13, 2026 When US tariffs threatened to slow growth, the government chose to invest in housing and infrastructure. The plan for the next four years: about 700 billion pesos for highways, 886 billion for passenger and freight trains, 794 billion for power generation, 2 trillion in Pemex's strategic plan, 180 billion for water projects, ports, gas pipelines, and about 3 trillion for 12 million housing actions. It also includes Coatlicue, a supercomputer meant to be the most powerful in Latin America.

🇲🇽✊ "Mexico contributed, according to the latest ECLAC report, 60% of the reduction of poverty in all of Latin America." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, 50th anniversary of the Business Coordinating Council (CCE), Mexico City, Oct 13, 2026 Speaking to Mexico's top business lobby on its 50th anniversary, Sheinbaum took on the line that "Mexico is not growing." She showed an OECD chart placing Mexico seventh in economic growth last quarter, above Colombia, Turkey, Poland, Latvia and the OECD average. INEGI reported 3.6% annual growth for August. She credited infrastructure investment with reasonable financing and mixed investment, plus Mexico's place in US electronics production for the AI boom.

🇲🇽⚖️ "If it is not complied with, then we move to the next step, which is no longer just a presidential decree, but a law." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 14, 2026 Sheinbaum signed a decree today requiring digital platforms to keep violent content away from minors' accounts: hate speech, violent extremism, sexual abuse and exploitation, suicide and self-harm, eating disorders, school violence and bullying. Platforms must verify age, set safe defaults for minors, give parents supervision tools, and keep a contact point for investigators. Meta, Microsoft, Apple, TikTok, Google, X and Huawei agreed in meetings and asked for one month to adjust. If they fail, a law with sanctions follows. Asked about hate speech, she said the decree "has nothing to do with political matters."
banner: META, GOOGLE, X: ONE MONTH TO COMPLY

text: 🇲🇽⚖️ "How is it possible that in 2026 there is still torture of young people by police?" "We, who come from fighting against repression, cannot allow there to be forces of order in Mexico that repress." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 14, 2026 Asked about abuses by state and municipal police in Guanajuato, including six University of Guanajuato students allegedly tortured after an arrest, Sheinbaum also returned to the case of young people tortured by police in Jalisco. She asked the National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) for a deep investigation: who gave the order, interviews with the victims, and people held responsible. She recalled that Morelos wrote the rejection of torture into the Sentimientos de la Nación, and that it persisted through the authoritarian PRI period.
banner: "THERE CAN BE NO TORTURE IN MEXICO"

text: 🚨🇲🇽 "What we have always said is: give us the evidence of why they say they are linked to criminal organizations." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 14, 2026 Excélsior reported on a US Treasury (OFAC) document claiming the Cártel del Noreste has decided elections and public works contracts in northern border municipalities. Sheinbaum explained that OFAC can act to stop transfers of money from Mexico to the US. When Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF) finds irregularities, accounts are frozen here too; when it finds no evidence, there is only the US sanction. "One thing is having an irregularity in an account, and another is knowing it is linked to organized crime." If the evidence is provided, prosecutors open an investigation. In this case, she said, Mexico's Finance Ministry has not found any link to a criminal organization.
📸 50th anniversary of the Business Coordinating Council (CCE) — Mexico City, 13 de octubre de 2026
